findings.title: Unsubscribe is a non-idempotent GET with no token
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is a logged-in GET that immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Mail clients, link scanners, and prefetchers follow GET links, and another site can trigger it with the session cookie (CSRF). The update is also not idempotent: watching/tracking is set to regular, and a second request (refresh or a scanner plus the real click) then sets muted. Users can lose topic notifications without choosing to, or land on a different level than the first click intended.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser exists
findings.body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(...) and then calls tu.notification_level with no nil check. Notification mail can be sent to a user who has no topic_users row (or the row can be missing for other reasons). Clicking the new per-topic link then raises NoMethodError and the user is not unsubscribed.

findings.title: Direct save skips reason flag, so mute does not stick
findings.body: The new action assigns notification_level and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips notifications_reason_id, notifications_changed_at, and the MessageBus notification_level_change publish. update_last_read auto-promotes to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and the user has viewed the topic long enough, so a mute from this link is undone the next time they read the topic, and other open clients never see the change.

findings.title: Watching users are not actually unsubscribed
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking or watching — the people who receive topic emails), the action sets regular rather than muted. The email copy says this link stops notifications for the topic, but regular still delivers mentions, quotes, and replies-to-you. Only a second accidental request mutes them. The level change also does not match the Ember page, which tells the user they will stop receiving notifications.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url
findings.body: server.en.yml unsubscribe_link always interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder appends I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is set. template_args only contains unsubscribe_url if the caller passed it. Any other mailer or plugin that sets add_unsubscribe_link without that option raises a missing-interpolation error and fails to send, or emits a broken link. There is no default, and List-Unsubscribe still points only at user preferences.

findings.title: Unsubscribe page claims success without unsubscribing
findings.body: The Ember topicUnsubscribe route only loads the topic, clears notificationReasonText, and renders stopNotificiationsText ('You will stop receiving notifications...'). It never calls the server to change notification level. The message is an unescaped HTML claim of a side effect this route does not perform. In-app visits, or a server action that stops mutating on GET, show a false confirmation while the user remains subscribed until they happen to use the dropdown.
